title: Chip Industry Week In Review
gist: Weekly chip-industry roundup: TSMC outsources CoWoS silicon interposers to GlobalFoundries ($2B, ramp 1H28), semis YTD sales top $1T by August, Brookings puts the US AI buildout at $10.3T through 2032, and export-control pressure shifts toward DUV immersion and optical interconnects. Also notable: 800VDC data-center power gaining an ecosystem, large quantum/power-tech raises, and Micron Taiwan strike risk.

insights.claim: TSMC and GlobalFoundries signed a $2B agreement under which GF will make silicon interposers for TSMC's CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem at its Malta, New York fab, with volume ramp expected in 1H 2028.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: TSMC is offloading CoWoS interposer capacity to a US partner, signaling persistent packaging bottlenecks and giving GF a new AI-linked revenue stream from 2028.
insights.quote: TSMC and GF inked a $2B manufacturing agreement, under which GF will manufacture silicon interposers for TSMC’s CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem at its Malta, New York fab.

insights.claim: Applied Materials and Intel are expanding R&D collaboration on next-gen transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging, linking Applied's EPIC Center with Intel's Hillsboro R&D.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Deepens Applied's position as co-development partner for leading-edge process and packaging roadmaps.

insights.claim: Rapidus launched Rapidus CORE, an ecosystem framework spanning design through manufacturing for its planned 2nm foundry, starting with 17 design-service partners.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Rapidus is building the design-enablement moat needed to win 2nm customers away from TSMC/Samsung; partner count is an early traction metric.
insights.quote: The first phase includes 17 design-service partners.

insights.claim: Xanadu and GlobalFoundries formed a multi-year partnership to move ultra-low-loss silicon nitride photonics and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors onto GF's 300mm line in Malta, New York.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: GF Malta is accumulating specialty AI/photonics/quantum work, strengthening its differentiation away from leading-edge logic.

insights.claim: Towa plans ~$32M for a new molding equipment plant near Kyoto and Elephantech plans an advanced packaging center in Tokyo for AI-server packaging and PCBs.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Packaging equipment suppliers are adding capacity, consistent with sustained AI-driven advanced packaging demand.

insights.claim: Global semiconductor sales reached $159.7B in August, up 8% from July, with year-to-date sales already above $1T according to SIA/WSTS.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Crossing $1T in under three quarters confirms an extraordinarily strong cycle driven by AI.
insights.quote: Global semiconductor sales reached $159.7B in August, up 8% from July, with year-to-date sales topping $1T, reports SIA/WSTS.

insights.claim: McKinsey expects inference to account for about 60% of AI compute by 2030, driving demand for custom accelerators, HBM, chiplets, advanced packaging and silicon photonics.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: An inference-dominant mix favors custom ASICs and the memory/packaging/photonics supply chain over pure training GPUs.
insights.quote: McKinsey expects inference to account for about 60% of AI compute by 2030

insights.claim: Brookings estimates the US AI buildout could require $10.3T through 2032 for data centers, power, networking and chips, while warning increasingly complex financing could obscure financial risks.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Flags off-balance-sheet/structured AI financing as a latent systemic risk alongside the enormous capex opportunity.
insights.quote: but it warned that increasingly complex financing could obscure financial risks

insights.claim: A Richmond Fed analysis listed in the week's reports argues the AI boom isn't showing up in US fab utilization.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Suggests AI demand is concentrated in a few leading-edge/packaging nodes while broader US fab capacity stays underused.
insights.quote: AI Boom Isn’t Showing Up in US Fab Utilization (Richmond Fed)

insights.claim: Nvidia, AMD, Micron and eight other companies committed a combined $2.4B in AI tools and compute credits to the US government's Genesis Mission.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Vendors are seeding government AI adoption, potentially locking in future public-sector demand.

insights.claim: San Francisco enacted a 45-day moratorium on building or expanding data centers to review energy, water, air quality, land use and community impacts.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Local permitting pushback is an emerging constraint on data-center siting.

insights.claim: The Center for Technology & Statecraft argues DUV immersion lithography is the strongest remaining chokepoint on China's AI-chip production, estimating Chinese-owned fabs held more than 330 DUVi systems by 1Q26, and calls for a China-wide DUVi export ban plus servicing and component restrictions.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: If adopted, broader DUVi and servicing bans would hit ASML's China revenue and service business.
insights.quote: DUV immersion lithography is the strongest remaining chokepoint on China’s AI-chip production

insights.claim: The Wilson Center says silicon photonics, CPO and optical networking are becoming the next US-China semiconductor battleground, estimating China holds 56% of global optical-transceiver manufacturing capacity.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Optical transceivers could become the next export-control/tariff target, with supply-chain risk for AI networking.
insights.quote: which estimates China accounts for 56% of global optical-transceiver manufacturing capacity

insights.claim: The US DOJ charged the owner of Earthmade Computer with smuggling over $300M of export-controlled GPU servers to China via Malaysia and Singapore using false end-user information.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Enforcement against Southeast Asia transshipment routes is escalating, increasing compliance risk for server OEMs and distributors.

insights.claim: CSET modeled more than 10 million scenarios and found ping-based location verification the most cost-effective way to detect diverted AI chips, though cost and complexity may limit it and pairing with physical inspections could help.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Location verification could become a mandated chip feature, affecting GPU designs and export compliance.

insights.claim: Qualcomm and Huawei signed a multi-year patent cross-license covering 5G, compute, AI and networking, and Qualcomm will separately acquire certain Huawei US patents pending approval.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Secures licensing revenue visibility for Qualcomm and reduces litigation risk with a major China counterparty.

insights.claim: ASML and Carl Zeiss researchers outlined a hyper-NA EUV architecture with NA of at least 0.75 that could enable ~5nm features, more than one-third smaller than high-NA, possibly ready in about a decade though commercial production is uncommitted.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Extends ASML's long-run roadmap and pricing power, but it is a decade out and uncommitted.
insights.quote: The technology could be ready in about a decade, although commercial production remains uncommitted.

insights.claim: Canon says its nanoimprint lithography is entering the final stage toward full-scale mass production.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: A potential low-cost patterning alternative for some layers; watch for named customer adoption.

insights.claim: Micron faces a potential walkout at its Taiwan facilities after workers voted overwhelmingly to authorize a strike over profit sharing.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Supply disruption risk at a key DRAM/HBM site, and labor demanding a share of boom-cycle profits.

insights.claim: Samsung is reportedly planning ~$3.9B of investment in memory-chip testing facilities in Vietnam.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Shows back-end memory capacity shifting to Vietnam.

insights.claim: Toshiba plans to invest about $380M to double HDD production capacity for AI data centers by fiscal 2027 versus 2025.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: AI storage demand is lifting even HDDs, a positive read-across for nearline storage suppliers.

insights.claim: Netlist and Micron settled and cross-licensed Netlist's server DIMM and HBM patent portfolio, ending all pending litigation.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Removes a legal overhang for Micron and crystallizes value for Netlist's IP.

insights.claim: 800VDC data-center power is gaining ecosystem support: Microchip and Navitas released an 800V-to-6V OCP rack reference design, Infineon launched a 27kW PSU and bought C2i for vertical power delivery, and Atomic Machines launched with $250M including a micro-relay to cut 800VDC power during faults.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: The power-delivery stack for AI racks (GaN, SiC, high-voltage DC) is an expanding addressable market for power-semi vendors.

insights.claim: Wolfspeed received a conditional commitment for up to $1.5B in 30-year US government financing to expand domestic SiC materials and wide-bandgap power-device production.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Significant government-backed liquidity for Wolfspeed's SiC expansion.

insights.claim: VEIR raised $110M for superconducting power delivery for AI data centers, and NovoLINC demonstrated a thermal interface material handling 400 W/cm² on warped silicon while keeping junctions below 90°C.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Venture capital is flowing into power and thermal bottlenecks of AI data centers.

insights.claim: DARPA advanced four companies to the final stage of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative: Atom Computing (neutral atoms), Diraq (Si CMOS spin qubits), IBM (modular superconducting) and IonQ (trapped ions).
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Government validation narrows the field of credible quantum modalities and vendors.

insights.claim: Quantum hardware funding is heavy: Oratomic raised $475M for neutral-atom hardware, Universal Quantum raised over $100M, and PsiQuantum got a conditional loan commitment up to $150M from the US Department of War.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Capital and government financing are concentrating in quantum hardware scale-up.

insights.claim: IonQ demonstrated a photonic interconnect linking a trapped-ion qubit with silicon-vacancy quantum memory at over 1,000 entanglement events per second, more than four times the prior trapped-ion record.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Networking progress supports IonQ's modular scale-out thesis.

insights.claim: Consolidation continued: Skyworks completed its combination with Qorvo, Microchip acquired Vorago, Navitas acquired Claros, Cirrus Logic acquired INVENTVM and Infineon completed C2i.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Analog/RF/power M&A is active, with targets concentrated in AI data-center power and specialized niches.

insights.claim: Samsung's System LSI is reportedly halting development of new automotive application processors amid cost pressures.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Signals retrenchment in Samsung's non-memory logic businesses, easing competition in auto SoCs.

insights.claim: DHS proposed charging schools $70k for initial OPT and $30K for subsequent periods, which could make it more expensive for chip companies to hire international engineering graduates.
insights.speaker: The SE Staff
insights.so_what: Rising US talent costs add to the chip-workforce constraint.
